What is Luma Dream Machine?

Video and image generation platform from a 3D/NeRF research company, with notably strong camera motion understanding and natural physics. The Ray series models generate video from text, images or keyframes, and Photon handles image generation.

Best for

Video with controlled, physically plausible camera movement.

Main features

  • Ray2 and Ray3 video models with strong physical realism and camera control
  • image-to-video and keyframe-to-keyframe generation (define a start and end frame)
  • Photon image model
  • Modify Video for restyling existing footage
  • camera motion concepts (orbit, dolly, crane) as explicit controls
  • Brainstorm ideation board
  • extend video
  • loop generation
  • API access.

Practical use cases

  • Generating a shot with a specific camera move
  • interpolating between two keyframes to create a transition
  • producing physically plausible motion for product visualisation
  • restyling existing footage
  • previsualisation.

Who is it for?

  • Filmmakers, motion designers, 3D artists, advertising creatives and developers building video features.

Pricing, free access & limits

Freemium credit-based subscription; separate API pricing

Plans described in the source

Free tier with limited monthly generations at lower resolution and watermarking. Lite around $9.99/mo (roughly 3,200 credits). Plus around $29.99/mo (roughly 10,000 credits). Unlimited around $94.99/mo with unlimited relaxed generation. Premier around $399/mo for the highest tier. Annual billing discounted roughly 20%. API priced separately per generation.

Free plan

Yes - free tier with limited monthly generations, watermarked.

Free trial

Free tier serves as the trial.

Usage limits to consider

Credit-metered per generation, scaling with resolution, duration and model. Free tier is watermarked and low resolution. Commercial use rights require a paid tier.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Camera motion control is the best in this group - the 3D research heritage shows in genuinely coherent spatial movement
  • keyframe-to-keyframe generation is a uniquely useful control primitive
  • physics and object permanence are more believable than most competitors
  • well-documented API.

Limitations to consider

  • Less complete than Runway as a production suite - no rotoscoping or editing toolkit
  • character consistency across shots is weaker than Gen-4
  • free tier watermarking blocks commercial use
  • clip lengths still short
  • prompt adherence for complex scenes is inconsistent
  • pricing tiers have shifted several times.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web, iOS
  • API

Languages

  • English prompts and interface

API access

Yes - Luma Dream Machine API, priced per generation, with good documentation

Integrations and exports

  • API
  • available through some aggregators (Adobe Firefly app, fal.ai, Replicate)

Evaluation notes

Keyframe-to-keyframe is the feature to evaluate first - it gives more deterministic control than pure text prompting and reduces wasted credits. Compare directly against Runway Gen-4 on your specific shot type.
